## editor.activity

What people, agents and scripts did in this editor: the activity journal of every command run (the latest 2,000, within 8 MB), oldest first after since. Each entry: {id, parent (the command that ran it), time (milliseconds since 1970-01-01 UTC), source (UI, Automation, CommandScript or Internal), client (an automation client's name), command, summary (in a few words, as the Activity panel lists it: the undo step with the entities' names, the error's first line, the warning, or done), mutating, playing (ran while the scene played), runningCopy (changed the playing scene's running copy, which play.stop discarded), parameters (parametersTruncated when too large to keep), status (Pending, Succeeded, Failed), result (a summary) or error {kind, message}, warning, durationMs, frames (of a command that took several), entities (that its undo step touched, at most 256) and entityCount, undoStep}. Page with since = the returned latest while more is true, or with newest: true (the latest first) with before = the returned oldest; editor.activity.export turns entries into a command script.

Kind: `Query` · Results: `Session` · MCP toolsets: `editor` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStateCommands.cpp:412`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `before` | integer | no |   | Return entries with an id below this (default: none). Value: at least `1`, at most `9223372036854775807`. |
| `command` | string | no |   | Only entries of this command, or of a group with a prefix ending in '.' (&quot;entity.&quot;). |
| `limit` | integer | no |   | Most entries to return (default 100). Value: at least `1`, at most `2000`. |
| `newest` | boolean | no |   | Newest first: the latest entries (default false: oldest first). |
| `since` | integer | no |   | Return entries with an id above this (default 0: from the oldest kept). Value: at least `0`, at most `9223372036854775807`. |
| `source` | string | no |   | Only entries of this source. One of: `UI`, `Automation`, `CommandScript`, `Internal`. |

## editor.activity.export

Writes the successful edits after an entry of the activity journal (editor.activity; since 0: from the session's start) as a command script for StrataEditor --commands, to repeat a session on a copy of the project as it was at that point, e.g. as a regression script: commands of kind Edit (editor.commands), also those run while playing that outlast play mode (materials, assets, scene.save), but not edits of a playing scene's running copy (play.stop discarded them: skippedWhilePlaying). Entities and assets the session created get new IDs every run, so the script binds them where a result gave them (&quot;bind&quot;: {&quot;e12.id&quot;: &quot;/id&quot;}) and refers to them where they are used ({&quot;\$ref&quot;: &quot;e12.id&quot;}); queries of the project's content whose results later edits took IDs from are part of the script too (IDs from results that follow the editor's session, such as selection.get and editor.status, stay as they are). Returns {path, steps, edits, lookups, bindings, skippedWhilePlaying, editsOutsideCommands, unrepeatableEdits, warning?, since, latest}: changes made outside commands (inspector fields, gizmo drags, the material editor record their undo steps directly) and the undo steps of commands a script does not repeat (scene.recover) cannot be in the script, and a warning says so when there were any. Fails when the journal no longer holds every entry after since (it keeps at most 2,000 commands and 8 MB of them: export from a later entry then), or when the parameters of a command the script needs were too large to keep.

Kind: `Session` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `editor` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStateCommands.cpp:504`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `overwrite` | boolean | no |   | Replace an existing file at path (default false). |
| `path` | string | yes |   | The .json file to write: relative to the project directory (needs an open project) or absolute; folders are created, network and device paths are refused. |
| `since` | integer | no |   | Repeat the edits after this journal entry (default 0: from the session's first command, which the journal must still hold). Value: at least `0`, at most `9223372036854775807`. |

## editor.batch

Runs several commands in this frame, one after another, as one undo step: steps \[{command, parameters?, bind?, expect?}\] as a command script writes them (bind names values of a step's result, {&quot;crate&quot;: &quot;/id&quot;}, and later parameters use them as {&quot;\$ref&quot;: &quot;crate&quot;} or {&quot;\$ref&quot;: &quot;crate&quot;, &quot;pointer&quot;: &quot;/entities/0&quot;}; expect checks a result like a failure). At most 1,000 steps; commands that can take frames (loads, builds, imports, captures, saves, play.step, input with wait: MayDefer) and editor.batch itself are refused before anything runs. atomic (default true): a failed step undoes the steps before it, records no undo step and fails the batch naming the step's index; atomic false runs every step and keeps what succeeded. Returns {steps: \[{command, result} or {command, error: {kind, message}}\], bindings}.

Kind: `Edit` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `core`, `editor` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: yes · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/Commands/BatchCommands.cpp:34`

| `steps` | array of object | yes |   | The commands: \[{command, parameters?, bind?, expect?}\]. Items: at least 1, at most 1000. |

## editor.perf

Where the editor's frames go: statistics of the latest frames the frame profiler recorded (at most 600). Returns frames (how many were summarized), frame (the CPU time of a frame without the waits for the GPU and the display, like the status bar's frame time), framesPerSecond, interval (the time from one frame's start to the next: what a frame-rate cap, vsync or idle throttling sets), stages (per stage of the main thread: Input, Assets.Update, Assets.Finalize, Scene.Load (swapping in a scene that finished loading, creating sub-scenes' entities), Scene.UI (the game UI's input), Scene.Scripts, Scene.Animation, Scene.Physics, Scene.Audio, Scene.Transforms, Render.Extract, Render.Submit, Render.UI (the game UI pass), Editor.UI and Present, plus stages modules registered; each its self time, nested stages excluded, with inFrameTime false for Present: presenting after the frame, and the wait for the display's image at the back buffer's first use inside it; neither counts as the frame's work), stageSum (the stages inside the frame time added up per frame), untimed (the rest of each frame, work no stage accounts for) and jobs (worker, I/O and background threads (imports, exports), how busy they were in percent, running and queued jobs now). gpu is the GPU's side of the same frames, known 2-3 frames late: frames (with GPU times), latencyFrames, busy (the GPU stages added up per frame), stages (per GPU stage: GPU.Uploads, GPU.Setup, GPU.Aerial (the atmosphere's aerial perspective), GPU.Cull, GPU.Shadows, GPU.Prepass, GPU.ScreenShadows (the sun's shadow mask), GPU.AO, GPU.RadianceCascades (global illumination: voxels), GPU.Reflections (reflection probes' conversions, screen-space reflections), GPU.Opaque (with the sky), GPU.Transparent, GPU.TAA (motion vectors' history and temporal anti-aliasing), GPU.MotionBlur, GPU.DepthOfField, GPU.Post, GPU.Overlays, GPU.UI (the game UI), GPU.ImGui) and boundBy: gpu when the GPU's median busy time takes at least 90% of the median frame interval and exceeds the CPU's frame time, cpu when the CPU's does, capped when neither does (vsync or a frame-rate cap sets the pace), unknown without GPU times. renderStats is the viewport's latest frame (null while it renders none): quality (the Graphics Quality it drew with, as project.settings shows Renderer.Quality), shadowMapSize (the sun's cascades' texels), cascades (each sun cascade's slice near and far in meters of view distance and texelSize in meters: stable cascades, which depend on the view alone), localShadowTileSizes (the tiles of the first 64 shadowed point and spot lights by rank), localShadowTileSizeCounts (how many have tiles of each size, by size in texels), gpuDriven (the frame took the GPU-driven path: its counts are the GPU's, of a frame 2-3 frames older, once gpuCounts is true; transparent surfaces are the CPU's), gpuCulled (the GPU culled the scene's mesh renderers and built their draws; false in a scene without mesh renderers, whose frames record no culling and take their requests from the CPU), feedbackRequests (its asset requests came from the GPU's visibility feedback of an earlier frame, not from the CPU walking the view), drawCommands (draw calls the CPU recorded), draws (instanced draws of the view), opaqueDraws, shadowDraws, instances, shadowCasters, triangles, visibleProxies, occludedProxies (in the frustum but hidden behind what the view draws: left out on the GPU-driven path), occludedCasters (shadow casters hidden from the light behind other casters, per cascade: left out of those cascades on the GPU-driven path), cachedCascades (shadow cascades kept from the previous frame: nothing reaching them changed), localShadowRequested (shadowed point, spot and rect lights in view, which ask for a shadow), localShadowLights (those given one: Graphics Quality's MaxShadowedLocalLights and the atlas decide), localShadowFading (those fading the shadow they lost out), localShadowViewsDrawn (their shadow views drawn: none while nothing reaching them changed), localShadowViewsPending, localShadowCasters, reflectionProbes (reflection probes the view shaded with), reflectionProbesPending (in view, their capture still loading or waiting to be converted), culledProxies, sizeCulledProxies (in view but below a pixel), instancesPerLod, lights, areaLights (of lights, the rect lights), areaLightShading (the forward passes used the shaders that shade rect lights, a little costlier: the scene has a rect light, lit or not, in view or not), areaShadowMasks (the shadowed rect lights whose shadows opaque surfaces took from screen-space masks, at most 4), areaShadowTiles (the atlas tiles the shadowed rect lights hold, six each), droppedLights, materials, pendingAssets, extractMs, sortMs, proxyUpdates, instanceBytesUploaded, deferredInstanceBytes (new mesh renderers waiting for their upload to the GPU), geometryPool (the meshes' GPU geometry: usedMB, capacityMB, allocations, fragmentation, moves, growths), sceneMirrorMB (the GPU memory of the scenes' GPU copies: a playing scene's doubles its scene's), exposure (what automatic exposure metered, frames late: ev100, EV100 = log2 of the metered luminance in nits + 3; keyStops, the exposure key's darkening, 0 or below; cardEv100, the EV100 of a gray card in the directional light's light, null without one; exposure is null with manual exposure), motionBlur (samples, tileSize in pixels; null on frames that did not blur), depthOfField (focusDistance in meters, focalLength in millimeters, fNumber, infinityBlurPixels: the blur's diameter of a point infinitely far; null without a lens), colorLookup (whether the Post Process's color lookup was applied; false while it loads), lensFlare (sunInFront: whether the directional light's disk was in front of the camera for the starburst; null when lens flares did not run), globalIllumination (ran, pending: its voxels incomplete, settled: nothing left to voxelize; null without GI), gpuMs (per GPU stage of the frame gpuStatsFrame names). gameRenderStats is the same for the Game view's latest frame (null while it is hidden or closed); both views' GPU work adds up in gpu's stages. Times are milliseconds as avgMs, p50Ms and p95Ms (nearest rank) and maxMs.

Kind: `Query` · Results: `Session` · MCP toolsets: `perf` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStateCommands.cpp:927`

## editor.quit

Closes the editor after answering (pending commands are cancelled). Fails while the scene has unsaved changes, the project file unwritten settings (its last write failed: project.save) or the preferences file unwritten preferences (preferences.save), unless force is true; save first with scene.save or scene.saveAs. Waits for saves in flight first, also with force: a save is never lost. Returns quitting, discardedChanges, discardedSettings and discardedPreferences (whether unsaved scene changes, unwritten project settings or unwritten preferences were discarded).

## editor.screenshot

Takes a picture of the editor's window as the person sees it, UI and all, or of one of its panels (panel, named as editor.showPanel names them), and returns it as a PNG image with its width and height; path also saves it. The picture is of the first frame, from the second after the command, that lays out its windows and tabs as the frame before (at most 30 frames later; settled false when the layout still changed), so the commands before it (editor.showPanel, editor.showDialog, selection.set...) show in it, and the window is read back without stalling a frame. What is still loading shows as the person sees it: wait first (editor.wait) after a start. Fails, changing nothing, for an unknown panel, a panel that is closed, hidden behind another tab (editor.showPanel brings it to the front) or asked for while the launcher shows, an existing file without overwrite, and an editor without a window (--headless, --no-gpu). Start the editor with --window-size &lt;width&gt;x&lt;height&gt; and --ui-scale 1 (StrataCLI launch takes both) for pictures that compare across machines. Returns {Image, width, height, panel, region: {x, y, width, height} (the window's pixels it shows), settled, path?}.

## editor.showDialog

Opens a dialog of the editor's window for the person at it, e.g. to show what you are about to do or for a screenshot: export (the Export Game dialog; needs a project), newProject (New Project, with template preselected), openSample (Open Sample: where to copy the sample, the first one by default; see project.samples), recovery (Recover Unsaved Changes: the project's recovery data that scene.recoveryStatus lists, for the person to recover or discard; needs a project, and closes by itself when nothing applies), newScript (New Script: a script class for the project's script directory, as script.create writes; needs a project), preferences (Preferences: the person's preferences that preferences.get lists, at section's page; works without a project), externalEditor (Preferences at its External Editor page: the program that opens script files, as script.setExternalEditor sets) or about (About Strata). The project dialogs ask about unsaved scene changes first. Changes no scene data and records no undo; fails in an editor without a window (--no-gpu or headless). Returns {dialog} and, for openSample, the sample it offers (sample), for preferences and externalEditor the page it shows (section).

Kind: `Session` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `editor` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/EditorLayer.cpp:389`

## editor.showPanel

Opens a panel of the editor's window and brings it to the front, e.g. to show the person at the editor what you are looking at: Streaming (asset memory per pool against its budget, loads, uploads, the assets), Performance (where the frames go, stage by stage), Problems (the last script build's errors and warnings, the scripts' crash with where it happened), Activity (every command the person, agents and scripts ran: editor.activity), ProjectSettings (the project's settings, page by page: what project.settings lists; needs a project), Console, ContentBrowser, Hierarchy, Inspector, AssetInspector (the Asset tab: the inspected asset, its settings and preview), Viewport (the Scene view; &quot;Scene&quot; works too) or Game (the Game view: the game through its camera); for the ContentBrowser, scripts: true shows its Scripts root (the project's script files with their classes, as script.list lists them) and false its asset folders; for the Hierarchy, search replaces the text of its search field as if the person typed it (a name, c\:Light, t\:Enemy, and in a world l\:Props or cell:3,-1; &quot;&quot; clears it). Changes no scene data and records no undo; fails in an editor without a window (--no-gpu or headless) and while the launcher shows (no project is open).

## editor.status

Overview of the editor; start here to orient yourself. The default answer is compact: engineVersion, project {open, name, path, fileState: written, writing or unwritten (its last write failed: project.save)}, scene {name, scene, modified, entityCount}, play {state, paused, pendingSteps, running}, selection {count, primary}, undo {undo, redo}, errors {unread (errors logged since the last log.read), scriptBuild {failed, errors}, scriptFault, importFailures}, assets {ready, loading, importing, scanning, failed}, saving and editor {launcher}. sections adds whole sections: engine (engineCommit, platform), project (directories, start scene, export settings, fileError), selection (with inspectedAsset), undo (position, count), sceneLoad (the scene scene.open or project.open is opening: {scene, startScene, state, progress}, null when none), memory (privateMB, workingSetMB and their peaks) and the sections of editor parts: automation (port, clients, connectedClients with the names agents gave, pending requests and commands), assets (memory and budgets per pool, streaming queue, uploads; see asset.stats), game (the running game's window requests, cursor, save directory and graphics: the Graphics Quality options in effect, where each comes from, and the players' saved options), recovery (the edited scene's journal of unsaved changes and how many recovery entries apply; see scene.recoveryStatus), world (the open world: {name, cellsLoaded, cellsLoading, cellsDirty, persistentDirty}, null when the edited scene is no world; see world.status) and editor (window, frame rate, GPU). sections: \[&quot;all&quot;\] returns everything.

Kind: `Query` · Results: `Session` · MCP toolsets: `core`, `editor` · Answers later (MayDefer): no · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStateCommands.cpp:748`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sections` | array of string | no |   | Sections to add to the compact answer: engine, project, selection, undo, sceneLoad, memory, automation, assets, game, recovery, world, editor, or all. Items are unique. |

## editor.wait

Returns after the given number of frames. Use it to let a playing scene run, assets load or the viewport render before the next command. Returns {frames} and, when the editor measures its frames (not when a test drives it without its EditorLayer), frameTimes: the CPU time of the frames that ran entirely while waiting (all but the first), in milliseconds {count, medianMs, meanMs, p95Ms, maxMs}, without waiting for the GPU and the display, so command scripts can check frame budgets with expect.

Kind: `Query` · Results: `Content` · MCP toolsets: `editor` · Answers later (MayDefer): yes · Waits for the asset scan: no · Registered at `StrataEditor/src/Editor/EditorStateCommands.cpp:898`

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `frames` | integer | no |   | Frames to wait (default 1). Value: at least `1`, at most `1000000`. |

<details>
<summary>Parameter schema of editor.wait</summary>

```json
  "properties": {
    "frames": {
      "description": "Frames to wait (default 1)",
      "maximum": 1000000,
      "minimum": 1,
      "type": "integer"
    }
  },
  "type": "object"
}
```

</details>
